17692566_78d7ff15.text: adult testosterone-treated GPR54 KO males displayed "female-like" numbers of tyrosine hydroxylase-immunoreactive and Kiss1 mRNA-containing neurons in the anteroventral periventricular nucleus and likewise possessed fewer motoneurons in the spino- bulbocavernosus nucleus than did WT males

17692566_c0b97b71.text: GPR54 mRNA is expressed in the periphery (pancreas, placenta, and testes) and throughout the brain (hypothalamus, habenula, caudate nucleus, nucleus accumbens, and amygdala) (Lee et al., 1999)(Kotani et al., 2001)(Muir et al., 2001). GPR54 binds natural ligands called kisspeptins, which are encoded by the Kiss1 gene and synthesized in several brain regions, including the hypothalamic arcuate (ARC) and anteroventral periventricular (AVPV) nuclei (Kotani et al., 2001)(Muir et al., 2001)(Ohtaki et al., 2001)(Gottsch et al., 2004)(Shahab et al., 2005). GPR54 and kisspeptins are involved in the direct regulation of the reproductive neuroendocrine axis
